gate.instructions: Is this article about the watched fighter? Judge by the main news the article is built on - what the headline and the article as a whole are about - not by whether his name appears or by what its first sentences say. Test: delete every sentence naming him; if the story still stands, it is not about him.

options.about_him: He is the subject, or the one being talked about: the new information in this article is about him - something he did, or said about himself or his own career, or something someone said, reported or predicted about him.
options.partly_about_him: He is one of several subjects and gets real content: a preview or feature on a fight of his covering both fighters. Also: another fighter's own news (an injury, plans, a statement) when the article itself ties it to a fight between the two of them, whether booked, or already fought and being discussed. A fighter only rumoured or calling him out does not count.
options.not_about_him: The news is someone else's. He is named in passing, as background (his past fight retold in another story), as one entry in a card, ranking or list, or only in links or navigation. Him talking about another fighter or the sport, not about himself, is also not about him - even when he speaks at length.

gate_fit.instructions: A question about the options, not about the answer. For whether the article is about him, the possible answers are: about him, partly about him, not about him. Does one of them fit this article?

options.fits_well: One of these answers describes this article accurately.
options.fits_loosely: The closest answer is only partly right: something about this article is not captured by any of them.
options.none_fits: None of these answers describes this article: a different answer is needed.

source.instructions: Whose words or act is the new thing this article carries about the watched fighter? The person it ORIGINATED with - never the outlet, website or account that relayed it. If a journalist or podcaster passes on what someone else said, the source is that someone. If several, the one the article's main news is built on. 'His' means the WATCHED fighter's.

options.himself: The watched fighter speaks, posts or writes.
options.his_team: People who work on his fighting: his coaches, trainers, conditioning staff, sparring partners, physio, doctor.
options.his_manager: His manager, agent or business representative.
options.opponent_side: A fighter he is booked against or publicly linked to a fight with - including the fighter who last beat him or whom he last beat, when a rematch is discussed - or that fighter's coach or manager. A champion who is also his opponent belongs here, not under promotion.
options.promotion: The promotion and its officials (the UFC, Dana White, matchmakers, the promotion's official channels), athletic commissions, official records.
options.other_fighter: Any other fighter not booked or linked with him, however famous - including champions of other divisions, friends and teammates.
options.media: A journalist, pundit, podcaster or analyst in their own voice, or the outlet's own writer; also a leak or report with no named person behind it.
options.fans: Fan reaction, social media crowds, comment sections.
options.no_one: Nobody's words are the news: an event is reported as fact (a fight result, a weigh-in) and nobody is quoted or credited with announcing it.

source_fit.instructions: A question about the options, not about the answer. For whose words or act the news is, the possible answers are: himself, his team, his manager, opponent side, promotion, other fighter, media, fans, no one. Does one of them fit this article?

options.fits_well: One of these answers describes this article accurately.
options.fits_loosely: The closest answer is only partly right: something about this article is not captured by any of them.
options.none_fits: None of these answers describes this article: a different answer is needed.

act.instructions: What does the source do regarding the watched fighter? Pick the one the article's main news is built on.

options.reports_an_event: Nobody's words are the news: something happened - he fought, weighed in, faced off, was booked, a fight of his was announced or cancelled.
options.speaks_of_himself: He himself talks about his own situation, plans, past, condition, fight or life - including how he rates himself, his own forecast for his fight, and what he wants next. Only when the source is himself. A reply to an attack on him is answers_for_him instead.
options.assesses_him: Someone other than him judges him: his level, chances, performance, condition, style, place in the division.
options.predicts_his_fight: Someone other than him gives a pick or forecast for a specific fight of his: who wins, how, in which round.
options.calls_him_out: Someone other than him asks to fight him, challenges him, or trash-talks him.
options.answers_for_him: A reply to an attack, a callout or a claim aimed at him - made on his behalf by someone else, or by him.
options.steers_him: Someone other than him says what he should do next: whom he should fight, whether a rematch should happen, when to return, which weight class - including demands made on his behalf.
options.gives_news_of_him: Someone other than him gives a factual update about him: his condition, recovery, training, whereabouts, mood or plans.

Does one of them fit this article?

fact.instructions: What new FACT about the watched fighter does the article carry, if any? A fact is something that happened or is set to happen, not an opinion about him. Choose by the article's main news. An interview, a press conference or a media day is a place where things are said, not a fact: if something said there is the news, choose that fact (a booking, a health issue, a return date, a career move), or none if it is only talk.

options.booking: A fight of his being set, offered, negotiated, discussed as likely, or cancelled.
options.result: The outcome of a fight of his.
options.fight_week_event: The routine of a fight of his, and nothing more: a weigh-in, a face-off, an open workout, the card order, start times, how to watch.
options.health: An injury, a medical issue, surgery or recovery.
options.return: When he will fight again or be available: a return date or a timeline.
options.career_move: Retirement, a contract, a move of weight class or team, a title vacated, stripped or awarded.
options.personal_life: His life outside the cage: family, childhood, home, hobbies, money, a life lesson.
options.none: Only opinion or talk: no new fact about him.

firmness.instructions: If the article carries a booking, a return date or a career move about the watched fighter: how firm is it? Otherwise answer no_such_fact.

options.official: The promotion states it, or he himself (or his official account) states it.
options.reported: A named outlet or journalist reports it, citing sources.
options.rumoured: Unnamed sources, a leak, 'talks', 'discussions', 'plans', or another person's claim about what the promotion wants.
options.no_such_fact: The article carries no booking, return or career move about him.
